type: str; title "Address of this schema"; examples ["https://goodrelax.github.io/gr-scheduler/spec/_source/grs-document.schema.json"]
text: The address where the latest GRS schema is published; every document holds the same address.

type: str const; title "Version of the shape"
text: The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of this schema last changed.

type: UtcInstant, required; title "GRS build that wrote the file"
text: The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the GRS build that wrote this file was made. It is only for debugging; to check whether a file can be read, use schemaVersion.
The data exported to MSPDI, and the data that only GRS uses.
Same as MSPDI Project.
Same as MSPDI Calendars.
Same as MSPDI Tasks, except that the WBS tree is given by Task.parentTaskUid and Task.siblingOrder. GRS makes ID, OutlineLevel, OutlineNumber and Summary from that tree each time it writes MSPDI.
Same as MSPDI Resources.
Same as MSPDI Assignments.

The task groups, each shown as one row of the task group panel and one row of the chart. taskGroupMembers says which tasks each task group holds. When GRS reads an MSPDI file, it makes the task groups from the WBS.
Which task group each task belongs to: one entry per task, from taskUid to taskGroupId.
How each task is drawn (shape, colors and outline width): exactly one entry per task.

One record per task that came from an imported MSPDI file: which file and which task in it, so that a later import of the same file updates that task instead of adding a copy. A task made in GRS has no record.
The plan as it was before: a saved copy of earlier task dates, matched to the current tasks by uid and drawn as an outline over them for comparison.
Comment boxes on the chart. Each one points at a task, a highlight box or a free point.
Highlight boxes: rectangles on the chart that mark a range of days over a range of task groups, drawn with a frame, a fill or both.

type: object; title "How the schedule is drawn when opened"
text: How the document is drawn when it is opened. Keys that always have a value are always written.

Display scale of the schedule drawing, in percent: at 100 every ...Px value is drawn as that many CSS pixels, at 50 at half size. It scales shapes and text together; it does not change the app header, the command palette or the browser zoom.
Text size step of the schedule: small, medium or large, which are 7.5, 8.75 and 10 CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. The document opens at this step; a reader who changes it edits the document.
Width of one calendar day on the time axis, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. Fit to screen sets it so that the whole schedule fits the width of the screen.
Vertical size of the task figures, as a ratio to the default size. 1 is the default size; 2 draws plan bars, actual bars and task name labels twice as tall.

How deep task groups with treeState auto open. A top-level task group is depth 1. With value N, task groups down to depth N are open, so rows down to depth N + 1 are shown; 0 shows only the top-level task groups, closed.
Where the view starts when the document opens: notDecided lets GRS choose, placed gives the day at the left edge and the task group at the top edge.
notDecided: no person has chosen a place yet, and GRS chooses one when it opens the document; placed: the other keys give the place.
The day at the left edge of the view.
Where the left edge falls inside leftEdgeDay, as a part of that day; 0 is the start of the day.
The task group at the top edge of the view. When that task group is deleted, scrollPosition becomes notDecided.
Where the top edge falls inside that task group, as a part of its step (its band height plus the gap below it), not in pixels; 0 is its top.

type: object {firstDay,lastDay,isFixed}, optional; when the property is absent: no fit span
text: The span of days, firstDay to lastDay (both included), that Fit to screen and picture export show instead of the whole schedule when isFixed is true. Absent means no fit span.
The first day of the fit span (included), in the time zone the chart is shown in (viewTimeZone).
The last day of the fit span; its column is included.
When true, Fit to screen and picture export show the fit span instead of the whole schedule. Opening the document does not move the view.
The time zone that the time ruler and the shown date-times use: sameAsScheduleData follows project.scheduleDataTimeZone, fixed uses the offset given here.
sameAsScheduleData: show the schedule data time zone, and follow it when it changes; fixed: show the offset given here.
The UTC offset that the chart is shown in.
Up to four extra clocks, each shown as one more row under the time ruler while the time of day is shown.
The UTC offset of this extra clock.
Whether this clock is the standard-time or the daylight-time zone of its offset. It picks the zone name that is shown; the offset itself is used all year.
Whether the time of day is shown on the chart; the stored date-times keep their time either way. A new document starts with false.
Whether plan bars are shown, apart from isActualVisible. A new document starts with true.
Whether the planned dates are shown to the right of each task name label. A new document starts with false.
Whether actual bars are shown, apart from isPlanVisible. A new document starts with true.
Whether the percent complete label of each task is shown. A new document starts with false.
Whether the earlier plan (baselineTasks) is drawn over the current tasks. A new document starts with false.
Whether the progress line is drawn: the line from the status date through the progress point of each task. A new document starts with false.
Whether progress markers and resume icons are drawn; while Delay Diagnostics is shown, markers are drawn even when this is false. A new document starts with true.
Whether dependency lines are drawn. A new document starts with true.
Whether the assignee label of each task is shown. A new document starts with false.
Whether vertical date grid lines are drawn. A new document starts with false.
Whether lines between task groups are drawn, on the chart and in the task group panel. A new document starts with true.
up stacks a task group's tasks so that the chart climbs to a goal at the upper right; down stacks them so that it descends to a goal at the lower right. A new document starts with up.
Whether the theme is monochrome. A new document starts with false.
Width of the task group panel, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100.
Whether the task group panel width is set by the number taskGroupPanelWidthPx instead of by dragging the panel border. A new document starts with false.
The state of the head of the task group panel (level 0), above all top-level task groups. collapsed draws no task group at all. A new document starts with auto.
The task groups pinned in a band at the top of the chart, to compare them with task groups far away. Absent means none is pinned.
How the three tables are shown: the Search Panel, the Delay Diagnostics Report and the Resource List.
How the tables of the Search Panel are shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
The tasks whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.
The column filters of the Search Panel tables (the task table and the comment box table), one per filtered column, by the column names of those tables. Absent means no column is filtered.

type: ColumnSort, optional; when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.
How the Delay Diagnostics Report table is shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
The tasks whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.
The column filters of the Delay Diagnostics Report table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column is filtered.

type: ColumnSort, optional; when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.
How the Resource List table is shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.
Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.
The resources whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.
Whether the (no assignee) row of the Resource List is checked. A new document starts with false.
The column filters of the Resource List table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column is filtered.

type: ColumnSort, optional; when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.

type: $ref DocumentStamp; title "Last change, last save and last writer"
text: The stamp of the document: when it last changed and was saved, and who wrote it last.

type: ChangeLogEntry[], optional, minItems 1; title "Notes on changes"
text: The change log: notes that people or an AI write about changes made to the document, oldest first. New entries are added at the end.
